title: PRD: Incident-derived acceptance matrix and runbook gating for KV/serving regressions
creator: Aisha Khan
description: After the recent KV cache regeneration incident (partial tenant latency spikes and degraded throughput), we need to convert postmortem action items into measurable PRD acceptance criteria. This ticket defines an acceptance matrix that ties operational runbook triggers and rollback gates to PRD sign-off, plus scope changes for the runtime and console to support automated canaries and traffic-shepherding verification.
background: Incident summary: KV cache rehydration under load caused sustained p99 latency increases for a subset of tenants during autoscale events. Postmortem recommended: explicit rollback gates, synthetic canary scenarios, tenant-fallback budgets, and observable runbook hooks. Existing PRD lacked concrete numerical thresholds and test harness definitions to validate regressions before rollout.
scope_changes: Add a new section to the serving PRD titled 'Operational Acceptance Matrix' with explicit SLO deltas, automated synthetic checks, and required console dashboards. Scope includes: runtime telemetry tags (traffic-shepherd markers), canary input sets, regression thresholds, operator runbook integration, and release gating for model/kernel changes. Excludes changes to billing or tenant contract language.
acceptance_criteria: PRD includes a table mapping postmortem actions to a verifiable metric, a responsible owner, and remediation timeframe
Synthetic canary harness that can inject traffic patterns reproducing KV-cache regen behavior with pass/fail thresholds
Automated rollback gate: if tail latency (p99) increases by >25% over baseline for 5m and error rate >0.1% for same window, release is blocked/rolled back
Tenant fallback budget defined: per-tenant degradation budget of X=0.5% request loss per 24h and documented eviction order
Console dashboards surface token-level cost, p50/p95/p99, and canary pass rate; alerting rules present in PagerDuty
Acceptance tests in CI that run canary scenarios against a staging runtime and fail the PR if regressions observed
work_items: Document acceptance matrix and attach to main PRD doc
Implement synthetic canary harness proto (ENG: create traffic generator + seed corpus)
Add alert rules and dashboard widgets to console (Console: create canary pass rate panel)
Define operator runbook steps and tie to PRD remediation timelines
Create CI job to execute canary scenarios on every model or kernel bump
test_plan: Run 3 full synthetic canary runs against staging with varied sequence length distributions; require >=95% pass across runs
Introduce controlled KV-cache regen during canary to validate runbook and automated rollback
Measure and record baseline p99/p95/p50 and cost per token; verify regression < 10% on p50/p95 and rollback if p99 >25%
Post-rollout smoke synthetic run within 30 minutes of deploy to verify canary at production scale
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: shadow releases for two days, small-tenant canary (5%), then ramp to 25% with automated telemetry checks. If any canary failure, execute automated rollback and run operator remediation within 60 minutes. Full rollouts require 3 consecutive passing canary runs.
notes: Consider integrating an OPA policy to prevent risky kernel swaps without canary sign-off
Need legal alignment if tenant evictions or QoS changes are visible to customers
Estimate assumes existing synthetic runner can be extended; otherwise add engineering buffer
review_feedback: PM asked to tighten rollback criteria to include operator confirmation for partial-fail scenarios
Design requested a clear UI affordance in Console for canary control and manual abort
Engineering suggested adding an internal feature flag to disable automatic eviction for high-risk tenants
